A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same conformal early-stopping method by the same authors. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching v1 Appendix A to v2 Appendix B.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix A report original experiments on six problem families, measuring runtime, suboptimality, explored nodes, and solution accuracy.

after.justification: V2 retains these experiments and adds original predictor comparisons, heuristic evaluations, convergence analyses, and distribution-shift and calibration-size experiments in Appendices A, C, and D.

M1.justification: Section 4.1 changes the calibration-rank prescription from (n+1)/(c+1) >= 1-alpha to n/(c+1) >= 1-alpha, which can change the selected stopping threshold. The LSTM architecture, covariates, weighted loss, and overall training/calibration/deployment procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions already evaluate the same six problem families; the abstract's change from five to six does not represent a new dataset. Appendix D.1 adds shifted test distributions for CFLP, GISP, MIS, and MVC by perturbing continuous generator parameters.

E2.justification: Beyond the retained Gurobi/COPT termination baselines, Appendix C directly compares the LSTM against a conformally calibrated Linear predictor and CP UB rate heuristic. Appendix A.2 also adds separate evaluations of SCIP Feasibility Pump, RENS, and Simple Rounding, substantially expanding the evaluated alternatives.

E3.justification: New protocols test Gurobi MIPGap values of 1%, 2%, 5%, and 10%, generated datasets with 1000 training instances, controlled parameter perturbations, and calibration sizes of 5, 10, 20, and 100. These extend the evaluation design; the original benchmark splits and budgets are retained. Newly specified Gurobi version and MIPFocus information do not establish changes to the original experiments.

E4.justification: V2 adds convergence and prediction-error trajectories for 20 instances per family, statistics comparing discovery and certification of optimal solutions, simpler-predictor comparisons, solver-tolerance sensitivity, distribution-shift tests, and calibration-size sensitivity. These address predictor necessity and reliability questions largely untested in v1.

E5.justification: Mean and standard-deviation reporting already existed in v1. Appendix D newly specifies 100 independently sampled test sets for the shift study and 100 calibration-set resamples for the calibration study, including coverage variability in Table 16. No increased run count or new seed information is established for the retained benchmarks.

E6.justification: All 48 distinct original benchmark rows are retained unchanged, but substantial additional results appear in Tables 3–4 and 11–16. For example, Table 12 reports MIS runtimes of 11.7 seconds for LSTM versus 207.298 for Linear, while Table 14 reports OTS runtimes of 74.212 seconds for Gurobi at 1% tolerance versus 96.2 for LSTM. These are new comparisons, not demonstrated improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: V2 adds Theorem 5.3 and a proof giving coverage bounds under total-variation-bounded distribution shift. It also corrects the off-by-one bound in Lemma 4.2 and Theorem 4.1's proof, restores a factor of 2 inside Theorem 5.1's square-root terms, and changes the suboptimality definition to use the incumbent objective U rather than g.

C1.justification: The central contribution and headline accuracy/speedup claims remain. V2 explicitly restricts the abstract's guarantee to new instances from the same distribution, corrects the benchmark count to six, and states in the conclusion that speedups exceed 60% on five of those six families.

C2.justification: V2 explains trajectory-level calibration versus repeated callback testing, discusses when an LSTM may be inadequate, and interprets calibration-size effects on reliability and runtime. Appendix D additionally acknowledges unavailable original generator parameters and the restriction of resampling studies to synthetic families. The original training-cost and distribution-matching limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies Gurobi 12 and MIPFocus=1 and documents the alternative predictors, perturbation mechanism, and resampling procedures. The original hardware, architecture, training duration, and code-access destination are retained. These disclosures do not establish that the original experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds work on learned presolving, GNN-guided predict-and-search, and Apollo-MILP, and expands the distinction from Clarke and Stellato's earlier heuristic-validation approach. The references also add SCIP and replace the Zhang optimizer citation with Kingma and Ba. Publication-year and venue updates largely concern already cited works.

P1.justification: The main section order and much of the prose remain intact. V2 makes focused terminology, notation, citation, and grammatical corrections, expands several explanations, and organizes the supplemental material into Appendices A–D, moving the original tabular results to Appendix B.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands the visual evidence with the 24-panel convergence Figure 5 and new tables for convergence statistics, heuristics, predictor comparisons, tolerances, and sensitivity studies. Existing benchmark tables receive numbered captions, and the duplicated MVC table labeled Maximum vertex capacity is removed. Figures 1–4 are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 corrects an important off-by-one error in the calibration argument and adds comparisons that directly test whether the learned predictor contributes beyond simpler calibrated rules. Repeated calibration studies and convergence analyses substantially strengthen the evidence for reliability and the proposed mechanism. Unexplained differences between Table 11's LSTM suboptimalities and Appendix B, plus incompletely specified regenerated datasets, limit some new evidence but do not outweigh these gains.
